title: Digenome-Seq
scope: Illumina explanatory Cas9 Digenome-seq schematic: genomic-DNA target context, in vitro target-site digestion, whole-genome sequencing, and alignment-based cleavage-site identification. Deletion/Wild type/Insert rows are preserved as depicted contexts without inventing a mutation-generation or allele-selection operation. A Cpf1 application is represented separately only at the level explicitly reported in its supplied abstract; multiplexing is acknowledged without assigning unverified operations. No executable protocol or historical-priority claim is extracted.

states.label: Genomic DNA containing Cas9 target-region contexts
features: Genome is drawn as a blue line with an unlabeled yellow highlight; the adjacent Cas9 target line provides target-region context, without an intervening extraction or amplification arrow.

Three parallel target-region drawings are labeled Deletion, Wild type and Insert. The deletion row is shorter with a black central tick; the wild-type row has a gray central tick; the longer insert row contains a magenta segment.

An unlabeled arrow leads from the Cas9 target line to these three rows. Its meaning as a physical transformation versus an explanatory expansion is unresolved; the rows are retained as target contexts without asserting their generation, sorting or pooling.
The diagram does not name a species; the original-method abstract describes a human-cell application. The material digested and sequenced is genomic DNA in vitro, rather than intact cells.

states.label: In vitro Cas9-digested genomic DNA (digenome)
features: Nuclease cleavage of genomic DNA generates fragments with recurring 5′ endpoints at cleavage sites; these fragments carry the cleavage-location signal into whole-genome sequencing.
The digestion panel repeats all three DNA rows and places a yellow, blue-outlined nuclease icon over the middle row. It does not explicitly show which rows are cut, discarded or selectively retained.
The icon represents the nuclease acting on DNA, not a library tag or a consumed DNA intermediate. No phosphate, hydroxyl, adapter or other end chemistry is specified in the drawing.

operations.label: Target site digestion
operations.description: Cas9 acts in vitro on genomic DNA, converting susceptible target sequences into cut DNA fragments. The diagram carries the Deletion, Wild type and Insert rows into this panel without establishing an allele-specific cut or selection rule. The preceding unlabeled target-to-row arrow has no specified mechanism and is not treated as a verified indel-generation reaction.
operations.mechanism: RNA-guided Cas9 nuclease cleavage, represented by the yellow, blue-outlined icon. Cas9 and its guide supply cleavage specificity; the DNA, rather than the nuclease, becomes the sequenced product. No guide assembly operation or end chemistry is drawn.
operations.information_effect: Cleavage position is physically represented by recurrent fragment 5′ endpoints. The primary abstract identifies this as an in vitro cleavage assay; cellular indel validation is separate.
